text: ἐκλεκτός, chosen out, selected, sometimes as substantive, of those chosen out by God for the rendering of special service to Him (of the Hebrew race, particular Hebrews, the Messiah, and the Christians): an adj. in 2 John 1, 13.
ἐκλέγομαι, I pick out for myself, I choose.
ἐκκόπτω, I cut out (off, away).
ἐκλογή, choosing out, selecting, choice (by God): in Ac. ix 15 a Hebraistic genitive, equivalent to ἐκλεκτόν.
ἐκλύομαι, I am unstrung, become weak, fail.
ἐκπορεύομαι, I journey out; I come forth.
ἐκτείνω, I stretch out (forth).
ἕκτος, sixth.
ἐκπλήσσομαι, I am thunderstruck, astounded.
ἐκπίπτω, I fall out, I fall off, I fall away: hence, in nautical language, I fall off from the straight course: of flowers, I fade away, wither away.
ἔκστασις (properly, distraction or disturbance of mind caused by a shock), bewilderment.
ἐκχέω, I pour out (liquid or solid), I shed. See ἐκχύννω.

ἐλάχιστος, least, smallest (Mt., 1 Cor. xv 9), but perhaps oftener in the weaker sense, very little, very small (Lk., 1 Cor. iv 3, vi 2, James): ὁ ἐλαχιστότερος, the smallest, the least important: εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν, it matters very little: ἐλάχιστον, adv. a very little.
ἐλαία (olea), an olive tree: see ἐλαίων.
note: Cross-reference is printed with the accent on the iota (ἐλαίων), although the headword it points to is printed Ἐλαιών; transcribed as printed.

text: ἔλαιον (oleum), olive-oil: ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως, oil of enjoyment, the oil with which the heads of guests at banquets are anointed, Heb. i 9.
ἐκφέρω, I bring out, carry out, sometimes (effero) out of the city for burial; I bring forth, bear, Heb. vi 8.
ἐλεέω (ἐλεάω), I pity.
note: Linked to the ἐλεέω entry, which gives ἐλεάω as a variant; the page also has a separate cross-reference entry: ἐλεάω, see ἐλεέω.

text: ἔλεος, pity, mercy.
ἐλεύθερος, free (opposite of enslaved, cf. 1 Cor. xii 13).
ἐλέγχω, (a) I reprove, rebuke: (b) I expose, show to be guilty, John iii 20, 1 Cor. xiv 24, Eph. v 11, 13, James ii 9.
ἐλεημοσύνη, abstr. alms-giving, charity: concr. alms, charity.
ἐλευθερία, freedom, liberty, especially a state of freedom from slavery.
ἐλπίς (oftener probably ἑλπίς), hope.
ἐμαυτοῦ, of myself.
ἐλπίζω (ἑλπίζω), I hope, hope for: the substantive following ἐν, εἰς, ἐπί with dat. or acc., is the ground of the hope, that which makes hope possible.
ἐμβαίνω, I embark.
ἐμβλέπω, I look into (upon).
ἔμπροσθεν, in front, before the face: sometimes made a substantive by the addition of the article; usually c. gen. in front of, before the face of.
ἐμπαίζω, I mock.
ἐμφανίζω, I make visible (manifest); hence, act. I report (inform) against, Ac. xxiv 1, xxv 2, 15; pass. (quasi-technical) I appear before.
note: "quasi-technical" is broken across a line at the hyphen; kept as a real hyphen.

text: ἐμπίπτω, I fall in, am cast in.
ἔμπορος, a merchant, trader.

ἐν, (a) of place, in; ἐν τοῖς, see ὁ: ἐν Χριστῷ, of mystic indwelling; (b) = εἰς, into, e.g. Mt. x 16; (c) of time, in, during, at; (d) of instrument, (armed) with, Lk. xxii 49, 1 Cor. iv 21, &c.; (e) amounting to, Ac. vii 14 (cf. Mk. iv 8 bis); (f) consisting in, Eph. ii 15; (g) in the department of, cf. 1 Cor. vi 2; (h) in the judgement of, cf. 1 Cor. xiv 11; (i) Hebraistic use, Mt. x 32, Lk. xii 8. For ἐν ᾧ, see ὅς.
ἐνδείκνυμι (in the middle voice ἐνδείκνυμαι only), I show forth.
ἔνατος, ninth.
ἐνδύω, I put on, clothe (another): mid. I clothe (myself), dress: hence, metaphorically, of acquiring qualities; = ἐπενδύομαι, 2 Cor. v 3.

ἐνεργέω, (a) intr. I am at work, work; (b) tr. I work, the acc. expressing ‘that which is worked’, effect. In N.T. the word is generally connected with miraculous interpositions; (c) in the passive always with non-personal subject, as ἐνεργεῖν always with personal, I am made operative (effective), I am made to produce my appropriate result, I am set in operation, I am made to work. Mid. absent from N.T.
ἐνδυναμόω, I fill with δύναμις (power) (almost = δυναμόω).
ἕνεκα, ἕνεκεν, εἵνεκεν, for the sake of, on account of: οὗ (neut.) εἵνεκεν, on account of which, wherefore, Lk. iv 18; τίνος ἕνεκα, on account of what, wherefore, why, Ac. xix 32.
ἐνιαυτός, a year.
ἐνίστημι: only in the intr. tenses, I impend, am at hand, am present: perf. pcpl. ἐνεστηκώς (ἐνεστώς) as adj. present.
ἐνκόπτω, (I introduce an obstacle sharply in the way of a moving object, cf. Eng. colloquial ‘I strike in’) I block, check, hinder.
note: Souter spells the headword ἐνκόπτω (unassimilated); same word as the lemma ἐγκόπτω.

text: ἐντολή, an ordinance, injunction, command.
ἐντέλλομαι, I give orders (injunctions, instructions, commands).
ἔνοχος (obnoxius), involved in, hence liable, generally with dat. (or gen.) of the punishment.
ἐνοικέω, I dwell in, am settled (stationary) in.
ἔντιμος, (held precious, hence) precious; honoured, honourable in rank, &c., Lk. xiv 8.
ἐνώπιον (vernacular, attested from saec. ii B.C.), before the face of, in the presence of; in the eyes of.
ἕξ, six.
ἐξάγω, I lead out, sometimes to death, execution (duco).
ἐξέρχομαι, I go out.
ἔξεστιν, impers. it is permitted (allowed), sometimes followed by acc. et inf.: ἐξόν ἐστιν = ἔξεστιν, the ἔστιν being understood in Ac. ii 29, 2 Cor. xii 4.

ἐξίστημι, ἐξιστάω, ἐξιστάνω (lit. I remove from a standing position), (a) in tr. tenses (including ἐξέστᾰκα), I astonish, amaze; (b) in intr. tenses, I am astonished, amazed; I am out of my mind, I am mad, Mk. iii 21, 2 Cor. v 13.
note: ἐξέστᾰκα is printed with a breve (short mark) over the second alpha, not a circumflex.

text: ἐξαποστέλλω, I send away out, I send forth (a person qualified for a task).

ἐξουσία, (a) power, authority, weight, especially moral authority, influence; in 1 Cor. xi 10 the authority which the wearing of the veil gives the woman, making her sacrosanct; c. gen. indicates over any one; (b) in a quasi-personal sense, derived from later Judaism, of a spiritual power, 1 Pet. iii 22, and hence of an earthly power (e.g. Lk. xii 11 and often, in combination with ἀρχή).

ἔξω, (a) adv. without; in ὁ ἔξω, &c. the adv. is equivalent to an adjective, τὰς ἔξω πόλεις, foreign cities, Ac. xxvi 11, ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος, the outer (physical) nature, 2 Cor. iv 16, especially οἱ ἔξω, the outsiders, the non-Christians; (b) prep. c. gen. outside.
ἔξωθεν, (a) from outside, from without; (b) outside, equivalent to ἔξω, both as adv. and as prep. (Mk. vii 15, Rev. xi 2, xiv 20, &c.); τὸ ἔξωθεν, the outside, &c., οἱ ἔξωθεν = οἱ ἔξω.
ἐξουθενέω, I set at nought, ignore, despise.

ἐξομολογέω, (a) I consent fully, agree out and out, Lk. xxii 6; (b) I confess, admit, acknowledge (cf. the early Hellenistic sense of the middle, I acknowledge a debt); (c) in certain passages there is a difficulty as to the sense: in Mt. xi 25 (Lk. x 21) the Vulgate (with the Sahidic) renders by confiteor, but modern scholars prefer either I give thanks or I praise.
ἐπαγγελία, a promise: see τέκνον.
ἑορτή, a festival, feast, periodically recurring: ποιεῖν ἑορτήν, Ac. xviii 21 = ἑορτάζειν.
ἐπαίρω, I raise, lift up.
ἐπαγγέλλομαι, (a) I promise; (b) I profess, 1 Tim. ii 10, vi 21.
ἐπαισχύνομαι, I am ashamed of.
ἔπαινος, praise.
ἐπερωτάω = ἐρωτάω simply, I ask, question.
ἐπεί, (a) after, Lk. vii 1 (v. l.), Ac. xiii 46 (v.l.); (b) for, since; (c) otherwise, Rom. xi 6. 22, 1 Cor. v 10, &c.
ἐπάνω, (a) adv. on the top, above; (b) prep. on the top of, above, over, on: met. of rule, over, Lk. xix 17, &c.; above, more than, Mk. xiv 5, 1 Cor. xv 6.
ἐπαύριον, to-morrow.
ἔπειτα, then, thereafter, afterwards.
ἐπειδή, (a) when, Lk. vii 1; (b) since.
ἐπέρχομαι, I come upon, sometimes with hostility.
ἐπέχω, (a) tr. I hold forth; (b) intr. (νοῦν being understood) I mark, pay attention (heed), note, Ac. iii 5, 1 Tim. iv 16: I delay, Ac. xix 22.

ἐπί, (a) c. gen. locally, on, upon; and so met. of that on which anything rests, e.g. ἐπ’ ἀληθείας, in truth: of authority over, e.g. Mt. xxiv 45: concerning, Gal. iii 16: in presence of, e.g. Mt. xxviii 14: at, in, Mk. xii 26: in (at) the time (period) of, e.g. Mk. ii 26; (b) c. dat. on, upon: near, e.g. Mt. xxiv 33: on the basis (ground) of, e.g. Mt. iv 4: on account of, e.g. Lk. v 5, ἐφ’ ᾧ (= ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ὅ, τι), in view of the fact that: over (cf. under (a)), Lk. xii 44: against, Lk. xii 52: in addition to, e.g. 2 Cor. vii 13: in, at, ἐπὶ τούτῳ, meantime, John iv 27: for, with a view to, cf. Ac. v 35; (c) c. acc. locally, on, upon, generally after verbs indicating motion, but afterwards more widely used, both lit. and met., ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, in the same place, together, in all, cf. Ac. i 15, ii 47: near, to, towards (after word expressing motion, and then more widely), both lit. and met.: against: in addition to (cf. under (b)), Phil. ii 27: of number or degree attained, as far as, e.g. ἐπὶ πλεῖον, ἐφ’ ὅσον: of charge, rule, or power over: concerning, e.g. Lk. xxiii 28: on account of, with a view to, Mk. xv 24, John xix 24: of time, for, during, e.g. Lk. iv 25: of time, about, e.g. Lk. x 35.

ἐπιβάλλω, (a) I throw upon, cast over, 1 Cor. vii 35, Rev. xviii 19 (v.l.); (b) I place upon; (c) I lay, with τὴν χεῖρα (τὰς χεῖρας), either with innocent, or with hostile, intent (= inicere manum [manus]); (d) intr. I strike upon, Mk. iv 37; (e) intr. τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος, the share that falls to (belongs to) one, Lk. xv 12; (f) intr. ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν, he set to and wept, Mk. xiv 72.
note: In τὴν χεῖρα there is a stray mark over the rho (between ρ and α); read as χεῖρα. The alpha of ἐπιβαλὼν is poorly printed but legible.

text: ἐπιβαίνω, (a) I set foot on, I step on; (b) I mount (a horse), board (a vessel).
ἐπιγινώσκω, I come to know by directing my attention to (ἐπί) him or it, I perceive, discern, recognize: aor. I found out.
ἐπιθυμία, eager (passionate) desire, passion: see ἐπιθυμέω.
ἐπικαλέω, (a) I call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name; (b) mid. I call upon, appeal to, address.
ἐπίγνωσις, knowledge of a particular point (directed towards a particular object); perception, discernment, recognition; intuition.
ἐπιθυμέω, I desire, long; ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπιθυμεῖν, Hebraistic, to long eagerly, Lk. xxii 15.
ἐπιζητέω, I seek after, search for, make inquiries about.
ἐπιδίδωμι, (a) tr. I hand in; (b) intr. I give way (to the wind), Ac. xxvii 15.
ἐπιδείκνυμι, I show, display, point out, indicate; I prove, demonstrate, Ac. xviii 28, Heb. vi 17.
ἐπιγράφω, I write upon, inscribe.
ἐπιγραφή, an inscription.
ἐπιλαμβάνομαι, I lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).
ἐπιμένω, (a) I remain, tarry; (b) c. dat. I remain in, persist in.
ἐπιλανθάνομαι, I forget.
ἐπίκειμαι, (a) c. dat. or c. ἐπί et dat. I am placed upon, am laid upon, lie upon, am imposed; I press upon, Lk. v 1; (b) absol. I press hard, Ac. xxvii 20; I am insistent, insist, Lk. xxiii 23.
ἐπιστρέφω, (a) tr. I turn (back) to (towards); (b) intr. I turn (back) (to [towards]); I come to myself, Lk. xxii 32.
ἐπιστολή, a letter, dispatch.
ἐπίσταμαι, I know, understand.
ἐπιπίπτω, I fall upon; I press upon, Mk. iii 10.
ἐπισκέπτομαι, (a) I look out, Ac. vi 3; (b) I visit.
ἐπιστάτης, master, teacher (cf. Dalman, Words of Jesus, Eng. tr., p. 276).
ἐπισκιάζω, I overshadow, envelop.
ἐπιτίθημι, I place upon, lay on: with ὄνομα, I add, give in addition.
ἐπιτιμάω, (a) I rebuke, chide, censure; (b) c. ἵνα, I warn.
ἐπιτρέπω, I allow, permit.
ἐπιτάσσω, I give order, command.
ἐπιτελέω, I complete, accomplish, perfect.
ἐπισυνάγω, I collect, gather together.
ἐπιταγή, instruction, command, order, authority (often of a god).
ἐπιφάνεια, appearing, manifestation (of a conspicuous intervention from the sky on behalf of a worshipper).
ἔργον, (a) work, labour (in the physical, originally in the agricultural, sphere); (b) moral action, deed, hence with adjectives or genitives defining its character.
ἑπτά, seven: οἱ ἑπτά, the seven (‘deacons’ of Ac. vi 3–6).

ἐργάζομαι, (a) I am at work, I work; (b) tr. I produce by work, put in force, give operation to, realize, e.g. Mt. vii 23; c. cogn. acc. ἔργον, ἔργα, Mt. xxvi 10, &c.; c. acc. βρῶσιν, I work for, John vi 27.
ἐπουράνιος (opp. ἐπίγειος), heavenly, in heaven: ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις, in the heavenly sphere, the sphere of spiritual activities.
ἐργάτης, a field-labourer; then, a labourer, workman in general.
ἐποικοδομέω, I build upon (above) a foundation.
ἐργασία, working, activity, work, service, trade, business, gains of business: δὸς ἐργασίαν (da operam), take pains to, see to it that you, Lk. xii 58; performance, practice, Eph. iv 19.
ἔρχομαι, (a) I go: with acc. of extent, ὁδόν; (b) I come: εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἐλθών, having come to himself, having come to his right mind, ‘having reasoned with himself’ (Sahidic), Lk. xv 17.
ἐρωτάω, (a) I ask (a question), I question; (b) (= αἰτέω) I request, make a request to; I pray.
note: The mark after "make a request to" appears to be a semicolon, as transcribed.

text: ἔρημος (the Latin heremus may be due to false analogy with heres, hereticus, &c.), adj. desert; hence, ἡ ἔρημος (sc. χώρα), the desert, to the E. and S. of Palestine: of a person, deserted, abandoned, desolate, Gal. iv 27.
ἐσθίω, ἔσθω, tr. and intr. I eat, I am eating; I take a meal: aor. φαγεῖν, to eat, but in Rev. x 10 = καταφαγεῖν.

ἕτερος (alter), (a) of two, another, a second: ἐν ἑτέρῳ (sc. ψαλμῷ), Heb. v 6; ὁ ἕτερος, the other, the second, τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ), on the second day, Ac. xx 15, xxvii 3; ἕτεροι, others, another group; (b) sometimes it does not differ from ἄλλος (alius), being used of more than two, other, different, cf. Lk. viii 6–8, 2 Cor. xi 4: in Gal. i 6 f. ἕτερος appears to mean another of the same kind, as contrasted with ἄλλος, another of a different kind.
ἔσχατος (ultimus), last: ἔσχατον, neut. acc. as adv., at the last, finally; ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου, at the end; ἕως ἐσχάτου, till the end.
ἔσωθεν, (a) from within, from inside; (b) within, inside: τὸ ἔσωθεν, the inner part, the inner element.
ἔτι (adhuc), (a) of time, still, yet; even now: οὐκ ἔτι, no longer, and similarly with other negatives; (b) of degree, even; further, more, in addition.

εὐαγγέλιον, τό, the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel: the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, &c.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).

εὐαγγελίζω, but far oftener mid. εὐαγγελίζομαι, I bring good news, I preach good tidings, with or without an obj., expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person, e.g. Ac. v 42).
ἔτος, ἕτος, a year: κατ’ ἔτος (καθ’ ἕτος), annually; ἀπὸ or ἐξ ἐτῶν followed by a number (Fr. depuis, Germ. seit, English for), lit. from . . . years.
note: The breathings on the second headword and on the word after καθ’ are hard to read at this resolution; their shape (and καθ’) indicate rough breathing, so read as ἕτος.

text: ἑτοιμάζω, I make ready, prepare.
ἕτοιμος, ready, prepared: ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες, being ready, 2 Cor. x 6, cf. ἑτοίμως.
